record.label: One persistent Gaussian mode and rooted energy induction
record.statement: The finite-word Gram induction adjoins formal orthogonal external modes ℓ,w to the endogenous rooted space. Echo parameter t=σ/2 realizes a requested seed angle σ through q(w), reusing the same mode at every seed gate and independent modes across vertices. The manuscript also evaluates ⟨h,Lh⟩ for finite spin–Weyl sums h and uses orthogonality of external and endogenous directions to pass the rooted energy, not only the vector Gram entries.
record.boundary: Equality of seed marginals or ordinary Gram convergence does not alone prove rooted energy convergence. The displayed L-pairing calculation is a separate ingredient.

aligned_passages.text: ### 8.4 Removing the seed controls without changing their joint law Seed removal must simulate one Gaussian variable per vertex, reused at all seed gates. Replacing each occurrence with a fresh independent Gaussian would change the circuit. The source proves a theorem for any already fixed finite seeded word and any energy tolerance, producing one finite ordinary word. Its proof works in the fixed-word tree limit; it does not take a degree limit simultaneously with its small parameter. [OpenAI (2026b), §5, “Removal of seed controls”][q-seed-statement]. **A small component supplies a large response.** Fix $b>0$ and $01$. The right side is $o(r)$: within each ordinary packet the relevant Hermitian expectation is real, distinct packet centres have overlap $O(r^M)$, and terms containing only special packets have size $O(r^2)$. The norm remainder is carried by unitarity; it receives no unproved occupation bound. The exact zero clocks then cancel the first-order displacement on ordinary packets, leaving $o(r)$ error there. The prescribed action on a normalized special packet has $o(1)$ error, multiplied by its $O(r)$ amplitude. These are the unequal accuracy requirements that the next echo uses. [OpenAI (2026b), §5, accuracy of selective probes][q-seed-selective]. **The estimates must hold on the next input.** The repeated echo uses more than the initial special norm in (8.1). Let $\mathsf N$ count particles in the top child Fock space. Call a family $(\eta_r)$ bounded smooth when $\sup_r\|(1+\mathsf N)^k\eta_r\|<\infty$ for every fixed $k$. At each stage between simulated gates, the source propagates a linear ordinary/special decomposition on every such family, with $$ \begin{aligned} u_r\eta_r&=\Psi_{O,r}(\eta_r)+\Psi_{S,r}(\eta_r),\\ \|\Psi_{S,r}(\eta_r)\|&=r\|\eta_r\|,\\ \Psi_{O,r}(\eta_r)&=\zeta_r A_r\eta_r+o(r). \end{aligned} $$ Here $|\zeta_r|=1$, and the low unitary $A_r$ and its adjoint preserve all these seminorms uniformly. A separate part of the induction transports the special insertion: $$ u_r^*Z\psi_{S,r}/r=w_r+o(1), $$ with the negative sign between a selective flip and its undoing. The norm remainders remain separate from the designated smooth tails; no occupation estimate is imposed on them. This forward estimate gives the insertion approximation used at the next gate. For $P=Y,Z$, the vector $\widehat v_{P,r}=A_r^*PA_r\mathrm{vac}$ is itself a bounded smooth family. Since $A_r\widehat v_{P,r}=PA_r\mathrm{vac}$, unitarity gives $$ \begin{aligned} \|u_r^*Pu_r\mathrm{vac}-\widehat v_{P,r}\| &=\|Pu_r\mathrm{vac}-u_r\widehat v_{P,r}\|\\ &\le\|P(u_r-\zeta_r A_r)\mathrm{vac}\|\\ &\quad+\|(u_r-\zeta_r A_r)\widehat v_{P,r}\|=O(r). \end{aligned} $$ The second term explains why an estimate on the vacuum alone would not suffice: its input changes with $r$. The scalar phase cancels in this comparison. This $O(r)$ estimate supplies smooth approximants for actual insertions; it is not divided by $r$. The singular echo instead uses the more accurate difference derived next. [OpenAI (2026b), §5, packet invariant and insertion-approximation lemma][q-seed-echo]. **The echo amplifies a controlled difference.** Consider a forward cost $t/r$, a selective flip of the special component, the reverse cost $-t/r$, and a selective undoing of that flip. The packet invariant transports the special component so that its contribution to the insertion changes sign. For the actual insertion directions before and after the first flip, it gives $$ v'_r-v_r=-2r\,w_r+o(r). $$ The Weyl product of the two costs is formed with these actual directions before making any approximation. Their large centres cancel, leaving a bounded displacement $$ \frac tr(v'_r-v_r)=-2t\,w_r+o(1). $$ Approximating each direction by a low component with merely $O(r)$ error before this subtraction would leave an uncontrolled order-one error. The remaining scalar Weyl phase is independent of the root spin and cancels in insertions; it need not itself converge. The second flip restores the transported special component so that the same construction can be used again. Mixers receive analogous selective compensations. [OpenAI (2026b), §5, packet invariant, insertion approximation and “One echo”][q-seed-echo]. In the limit, $\ell_r$ and $w_r$ become two orthogonal external real Gaussian modes at each root. The initialization uses $q(\ell)$ and every simulated seed gate uses the same $q(w)$: choosing $t=\sigma/2$ implements $e^{-i\sigma Zq(w)}$. Different vertices have independent local copies. This is the required joint law of the seeded word. A finite induction uses the Weyl identity $$ \langle W(f)\Omega,W(g)\Omega\rangle =\exp\!\left(-\tfrac12\|g-f\|^2 +i\operatorname{Im}\langle f,g\rangle\right) $$ to match the relevant finite Gram matrices. Escaping high directions supply precisely the vanishing pairings between the new external modes and endogenous child directions. [OpenAI (2026b), §5, external-mode limit][q-seed-gram]. **The energy pairing after seed removal.** Matching the seed law and its finite Gram matrices is not yet enough. For a centred low insertion $h=\sum_j s_j\otimes W(f_j)\Omega$, the one-particle coefficient of $W(f_j)\Omega$ is $i e^{-\|f_j\|^2/2}f_j$. Hence $$ \langle h,\mathsf Lh\rangle =-i\sum_j\langle s_j,+\rangle e^{-\|f_j\|^2/2} \langle f_j,h\rangle. $$ In the seeded representation, $\mathsf L$ places the root-seed factor in its vacuum and creates $h$ only in the endogenous child space. External components therefore contribute zero to the last pairing. The high-direction estimate yields the same zeros in the actual limit. The actual insertion differs from its low insertion by $O(r)$, so energy continuity completes the comparison. Matching Gram matrices without this one-particle calculation would not identify $\mathsf L$ or its energy. [OpenAI (2026b), §5, “Finite Gram induction,” including the energy calculation][q-seed-gram]. **Why the selective rotations are available at every required stage.** The limiting projection of each special centre must be nonzero. The source imposes finitely many visibility conditions on the angles of the formal seeded word. At each relevant standard stage they have form $$ -2\operatorname{Im}\langle v_Z^{\rm form}, -2bz\,e+yD^{\rm form}\rangle\ne0, \qquad z,y\in\{\pm1\}, $$ where $e=Z\mathrm{vac}$ and $D^{\rm form}$ accumulates echoes whose reverse costs have already occurred. These functions are real analytic by the finite Weyl formulas. Setting all target angles to zero, while retaining initialization, gives $4bz e^{-8b^2}\ne0$, so none is identically zero. An arbitrarily small angle perturbation avoids their finite union of zero sets and the zero echo-time hyperplanes. The huge-cost stages need a separate transverse-projection estimate; their limiting projection pairs then also have a nonzero coordinate. Finite pulse lists can now be chosen successively from limits already established at earlier stages. No list is chosen from a limit that assumes its own successful implementation. [OpenAI (2026b), §5, huge-stage transverse projection, visibility and construction order][q-seed-visibility]. The choices are therefore nested: make $b$ small to control initialization; perturb the fixed target angles to ensure visibility; choose all finite probe lists; finally choose $r$ small. A value of $r$ fixes every large angle and every finite product. The theorem allows those angles to be large or negative. It makes no claim of uniform bounds as the target word length grows or as the tolerance tends to zero. [OpenAI (2026b), §5, proof of seed removal][q-seed-visibility].
